# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — CPT 63030 (Lower Back Disc Surgery / Decompression)

**Re: Cigna Medical Coverage Policies - Musculoskeletal: CMM-606 Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy, Laminectomy, or Hemilaminectomy) (V1.0.2026)**
Policy URL: https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-606%20Lumbar%20Microdiscectomy_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.30.2026.pdf

**Member:** Taylor Jennings
**Member ID:** W530749089
**Denial date:** 2026-07-31
**Reference number:** POC-F7C299C469-49918
**Payer/Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Illinois

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030), which was denied on 2026-07-31 as not medically necessary. I am asking that this decision be reconsidered. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is needed based on my imaging, my exam findings, and the treatment I have already tried.

## Why I believe my records meet the plan's own criteria

**1. Credentialed spine surgeon requirement.**
The policy states:

> "Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V1.0.2026 Credentialed Spine Surgeon Required • Endoscopic lumbar discectomy requires the procedure be performed by a spine surgeon with surgical privileges at a hospital, hospital outpatient department, or ambulatory surgery center to perform open surgical approach(es) for lumbar discectomy."

My surgery is being performed by Dr. Okafor, an orthopedic surgeon. [Please confirm/insert Dr. Okafor's surgical privileges and facility credentialing status, if not already in the prior authorization packet.] I ask that this be verified against the record rather than treated as a basis for denial without confirmation.

**2. Initial primary lumbar microdiscectomy — medical necessity pathway.**
The policy states:

> "Initial Primary Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy, Laminectomy or Hemilaminectomy) CMM.SP.IN.606.2 v1.0.2026 Initial primary lumbar microdiscectomy (laminotomy, laminectomy, or hemilaminectomy) is considered medically necessary when performed for EITHER of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met:"

The specific bulleted findings under this section were not included in the materials available to me, so I cannot quote them here, but I want to lay out the clinical findings that I believe are directly relevant to this section:

- MRI of the lumbar spine on 2026-06-08 showed an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- I have had 14 months of progressive lower back pain that does not resolve with rest, with radicular pain into my right calf.
- I completed 12 weeks (16 visits) of supervised physical therapy, including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, from 2026-04-10 to 2026-07-03, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for 6 months without adequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-20 gave only about 2 weeks of partial relief.
- I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes without pain.
- On exam, I had positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the level shown on my MRI.
- I have no active infection and no untreated substance use, which the notes also confirm.

I am asking Cigna to review these findings against the full text of CMM.SP.IN.606.2, including the specific criteria that were not provided to me, since the imaging, the failed conservative care, and the exam findings described above appear to be exactly the kind of evidence this section of the policy is designed to evaluate.

**3. Urgent/emergent pathway.**
The policy also describes an urgent/emergent pathway with its own criteria, including:

> "◦ cauda equina syndrome (CES) ◦ progressive neurological deficit documented on two separate physical exams ◦ neurocompressive pathology with ANY of the following:"

and

> "▪ motor weakness of grade 3/5 or less of specified muscle(s) ▪ rapidly progressive symptoms of motor loss ▪ bowel incontinence ▪ bladder incontinence/retention ◦ epidural hematoma ◦ infection (e.g., discitis, epidural abscess, osteomyelitis) ◦ primary or metastatic neoplastic disease causing pathologic fracture, cord compression, or instability ◦ a condition otherwise meeting criteria listed in the applicable procedure section(s) with documentation of severe debilitating pain and/or dysfunction to the point of being incapacitated CMM-606:"

I am not asking Cigna to treat my case under the urgent/emergent pathway, since my records reflect one documented exam rather than two separate ones showing progressive deficit. I am including this section only so the reviewer can see that my case was evaluated, and is being appealed, under the standard initial-procedure pathway described above (CMM.SP.IN.606.2), not the urgent/emergent one.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Cigna to reconsider the denial of CPT 63030 in light of the imaging findings, the documented failure of conservative treatment, and the exam findings in my chart, measured against the plan's own criteria for initial primary lumbar microdiscectomy. I am also asking Cigna to confirm Dr. Okafor's surgical privileges as described in the credentialed spine surgeon requirement, since this appears to be a documentation matter rather than a clinical one.

I understand this appeal does not guarantee that the decision will be reversed, but I believe my records support reconsideration.

## Deadline and how I am submitting this appeal

This appeal must be received by 2027-01-27. I am submitting it by logging in at my.cigna.com to locate my plan's appeal form, and/or by mailing it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and/or by calling 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my member ID card to confirm the correct submission method.
